'''Michael Christopher Payne''' {{postnom|country=GBR|FRS|HonFInstP}} is a British [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]], working in the field of [[computational physics]] and theoretical [[condensed matter physics]] at the [[University of Cambridge]].

He is the creator of first principles total energy pseudopotential code [[CASTEP]]<ref>[http://www.castep.org/CASTEP/CASTEP CASTEP people] retrieved 12 Feb 2017</ref> and has been involved in the development of the linear scaling code [[ONETEP]].<ref>[https://onetep.org/people/ ONETEP people] retrieved 12 Feb 2017</ref>
He was the 23rd most highly cited physical scientist in the UK between 1990 and 1999, and has published more than 250 papers which have had over 22,000 citations.<ref>[http://www.phy.cam.ac.uk/directory/paynem Mike Payne, University of Cambridge] retrieved 12 Feb 2017</ref>

He studied at [[Pembroke College, Cambridge]] as an undergraduate and PhD student. He then spent a year in [[John Joannopoulos]]'s group in the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] before returning to Pembroke College as a research fellow, and to the Theory of Condensed Matter (TCM) group in the [[Cavendish Laboratory]] where he had earlier completed his PhD. He became a university lecturer in 1994, a reader in 1998 and a professor in 2000.<ref>[https://www.phy.cam.ac.uk/system/files/documents/MikePayneCV.pdf Mike Payne, CV] retrieved 13 Feb 2024</ref> In 2019 he became the first holder of the [[Ray Dolby]] Fellowship in Physics at Pembroke College.<ref>[https://www.pem.cam.ac.uk/college/news/ray-dolby-fellowship-physics-announced Announcement of Ray Dolby Fellowship] retrieved 13 Feb 2024</ref>

He was awarded the 1996 [[Maxwell Medal and Prize]] by the [[Institute of Physics]] and gave the 1998 Mott Lecture. He was elected Fellow of the Royal Society in 2008<ref>[https://royalsociety.org/people/michael-payne-12060/ Michael Payne, Royal Society] retrieved 12 Feb 2017</ref> and awarded the [[Swan Medal and Prize]] by the [[Institute of Physics]] in 2014.<ref>[http://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold/swan/medallists/page_63425.html Mike Payne, 2014 IoP Swan Medal] retrieved 12 Feb 2017</ref> In 2011 he was made an honorary fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref>[http://www.iop.org/about/awards/hon_fellowship/hon_fellows/page_51382.html Mike Payne, Honorary Fellow (IoP)] retrieved 12 Feb 2017</ref>
He succeeded [[Peter Littlewood]] as head of the TCM group in the Cavendish Laboratory, a post he held until 2013 when he was succeeded by [[Benjamin Simons]].
